Every command and what it does.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `specbook init` | Scaffolds the config, the `#api/*` import and an environments folder. |
| `specbook add <service> --spec <path or url>` | Registers a spec and generates its code. An address is downloaded to `openapi/` and recorded in `openapi/sources.json`. |
| `specbook add --refresh [service...]` | Downloads the recorded addresses again, reports what changed and regenerates. |
| `specbook generate [service...]` | Generates types, operations, examples and metadata from the specs. `dev`, `build` and `test` do it when needed. |
| `specbook dev [--port n]` | Opens the docs, a play panel and a credential proxy, so you can run requests as you write them. |
| `specbook build [--out dir] [--minimal] [--viewer]` | Builds a static docs site and `specbook.js`. `--minimal` publishes only what your requests and flows use, and `--viewer` adds the spec viewer. |
| `specbook test [glob...]` | Runs requests and flows against an environment. |
| `specbook bundle [--out file] [--tag t]` | Compiles the tests into one `.mjs` that runs with just node. |
| `specbook check` | Validates specs, generated code drift, imported operations, placeholders and environment files. |
| `specbook secrets [--env name]` | Shows where each secret resolves from. |
| `specbook preview <url or file>` | Opens any OpenAPI document in the UI, with no project. |

## `specbook test`

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--env <name>` | Chooses the environment. The default is `mock`, for development. |
| `--tag <tag>`, `--grep <re>`, `--grep-invert <re>` | Choose what runs, by tag or by file and title. |
| `--list` | Prints what would run. |
| `--shard i/n`, `--bail n` | Splits a run into parts, or stops after n failed flows. |
| `--retries n` | Runs a failed flow again. A pass on a retry is marked flaky and exits 0. |
| `--timeout ms`, `--global-timeout ms` | Limit each request (default: the config's `timeoutMs`, else 30000; `0` waits), and the whole run. |
| `--safe` | Refuses requests that may change data. Use it against production. |
| `--reporter list\|json\|junit\|github\|ndjson[:path]` | Chooses reporters. Repeat the flag to use several. |
| `--input k=v`, `--var k=v` | Sets a flow input, or a variable. A variable can override an address. |

Exit codes: 0 when everything passed, 1 when a flow failed or errored, 2 when the run could not start (missing
secrets, a missing spec, an import that is not an operation) and 3 for a usage error.

`.specbook/specbook.config.ts` holds:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | The project's name. |
| `vars` | Defaults for every environment, such as each API's address. |
| `environments` | Variables for one environment, and a `risk` of `production` or `sandbox` where the name does not say. |
| `services` | `{ spec, baseUrl, auth }` for each API. `baseUrl` is a template like `'{{petstoreUrl}}'`. |
| `timeoutMs` | How long a request waits for an answer, in the CLI and in the browser. Default 30000; `0` waits as long as it takes. |
| `auth` | Profiles that apply a credential, such as headers built from `{{secrets.NAME}}`, or an OAuth flow. |
| `secrets` | The secrets the project uses, by name. |
| `faker` | `{ locales, default }`, the locales generated values can use. |
| `branding` | The name, title, tagline, logo, accent colors and links of a published site. |
| `codegen` | `outDir` and `importPrefix`, if the defaults (`.generated` and `#api`) do not suit. |

## The play panel

`specbook build` writes `specbook.js` next to your docs. Load it on any page and mark what should run:

<Snippet file="snippets/embed.html" region="embed" title="docs.html" />

A plain element gets a Play button beside it. A button or link that carries the attribute opens the panel itself.

| Attribute | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `data-specbook-try="service/Operation"` | Opens a request. A bare `Operation` works when the build has one service. A request file such as `requests/petstore/find-pets.req.ts` opens that saved request, with its checks. |
| `data-specbook-flow="id"` | Opens a flow by its id. |
| `data-specbook-example="name"` | Starts from a named example. |
| `data-specbook-inputs='{"quantity":2}'` | Sets a flow's inputs, over their defaults. |
| `data-specbook-env="demo"` | Chooses the environment. Set it on an element or on any ancestor, so a page can set it once. |
| `data-specbook-tab="docs"` | Opens on the Docs tab instead of Try. |
| `data-specbook-auto-run` | Runs as soon as the panel opens. Never against production. |
| `data-specbook-theme="light"` | Pins the theme. `host` (the default) follows the page, and `auto` follows the visitor's system. |

The panel is a dialog on a desktop and a sheet from the bottom on a phone. It follows the page's light or dark
theme and keeps what a visitor types out of the page's storage. The script also fires `specbook:open` and
`specbook:close` on the trigger, and exports `open` and `close`.

## Content-Security-Policy

The script works under `script-src 'self'`, with no eval and no inline `<style>` element. The code editors set
inline `style` attributes, so a strict policy also needs `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`.

## The whole viewer

The viewer opens any OpenAPI address inside your page. On your own origin there is no CORS, and your visitor's
cookies are sent.

<Snippet file="snippets/embed.html" region="viewer" title="docs.html" />

`spec` may be a relative address, and `baseUrl` sets the API address when the document has none.

| Situation | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| It is your API | Embed the viewer in your docs route. It runs on your origin, so there is no CORS and cookies are sent. |
| Your policy blocks third-party scripts | Self-host the viewer. The built folder ships in `@specbook/ui` as `dist-viewer/`. |
| You want the hosted viewer in your page | An iframe of `ui.specbook.dev` works, but it is cross-origin, so the API must allow it. |
| It is someone else's API | It works when that API allows calls from a browser. |
Where each API lives in each environment, and where credentials come from.

## Environments

`vars` in the config are the defaults for every environment. To change them for one environment, put them in
`.specbook/environments/<env>.env`, or under `environments.<env>.vars` in the config. A service's address is a
variable, so each environment can point somewhere else:

```ts
services: { petstore: { spec: './openapi/petstore.json', baseUrl: '{{petstoreUrl}}' } }
```

```sh
# .specbook/environments/staging.env
petstoreUrl=https://staging.petstore.example/api/v3
```

## Secrets

Name your secrets in the config, for example `secrets: { PETSTORE_API_KEY: {} }`. Specbook reads each one from an
environment variable first, then from `--secrets-file`, the environment's `<env>.secrets.env` and
`secrets.local.env`. The folder's `.gitignore` keeps the secrets files out of your repository.

Run `specbook secrets --env staging` to see where each secret resolves from. It never prints a value. A test run
masks every secret value wherever it appears, including its URL-encoded, JSON-escaped and base64 forms, and removes
credentials from reports.

## In a browser

A published portal never holds a secret. A visitor types credentials once per tab, they are kept per API origin, and
a key typed for one API is never sent to another. An embed keeps them in memory only.

## Addresses on the same origin

A relative address such as `/api/petstore` resolves against the page, so one environment file serves every host a
site is published on. This site's demo environment works that way.

A page that embeds the viewer or the play panel can restyle it from its own stylesheet. Light and dark follow the
visitor's system, and `data-theme="light"` or `"dark"` on the root forces one.

<Snippet file="snippets/theme.css" region="theme" title="site.css" />

The variables cover surfaces (`--sb-bg`, `--sb-surface`, `--sb-border`), text, accent, status colors, one color per
HTTP method, code colors, fonts, radii and spacing. For changes to its structure, the play panel also exposes
`::part(panel)`, `::part(header)`, `::part(timeline)` and `::part(play)`.
